items.title: Theodore Purnell Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: Professor Nickerson. He caught stumbling all around in my little client case one day... she had a little band there... they called his daughter, Camille... she'd sit there and play it long with it

ctx.x: What do you think has caused the change between those days and nowadays? Well, now, I tell you, time is a little faster. Time is a little faster, but some of the boys, they don't read enough.

They don't read enough. Now, Dad, you take right now, a boy get an instrument right now, cry out of the cypher, and I say in three or four months he's playing. Yeah, he's playing. He's playing. Do you know I took a lesson on a client at about eight years old? I took a lesson on a client at about two years, I think, before they even let me play a piece, Professor Nickerson. He caught stumbling all around in my little client case one day, and said for my dad, he said, you want to make a musician out of me? He said,…

With the ball and this is violin. Yeah. Yeah. That's some good things. See, the musicians they got now, they play. They don't know the chords to them. No, but if a fella go take lessons. They got some good little young musicians. Oh yeah, yeah. They can read up a little song. But most of them, those kind though, you can't get them. If a fella go take lessons now, what do they ask you?
